correctness.rationale: For x=(t,z), |t|<=delta=1-a, perpendicular cross-section is an (n-1)-ball of squared radius 1-(a+|t|)^2. Its coordinate variance is radius²/(n+1). Slice integrals yield axial delta² B2/B0. Integration by parts of (1-(a+t)^2)^{(n+1)/2} against t makes the perpendicular variance equal axial plus a delta B1/B0, and implies gap=a E|X1|. Let nu_a(ds) ∝ s (1-s)^k(1+a+delta s)^k ds; the derivative of log weight g_a(s)=k(1-s)/(1+a+delta s) is strictly decreasing in s, so d_a(B2/B1)=Cov_nu(s,g_a(s))<0. Thus B1/B2 strictly increases and so does A=1+a B1/(delta B2). The exact endpoint beta integrals give c_n and (n+5)/4. Thin-lens beta ratios give axial~8 delta²/[(n+3)(n+5)] and transverse~2delta/(n+3). Independent rational n=3 moment polynomials matched every displayed exact eigenvalue. No finite sampling is used to prove all-n monotonicity.
